findings.summary: Sample check R1: Requirement/AT1 specify plan_package_final.json plus an associated structured handoff bundle as the sole canonical planning input, but M1 deliverables only explicitly mention validating/recording plan_package_final.json; the plan does not explicitly state that the structured handoff bundle is validated and persisted as part of intake deliverables/checks.

evidence.note: R1 includes 'plan_package_final.json (plus its associated structured handoff bundle)' as sole canonical planning input
AT1 run (a) includes 'plan_package_final.json plus its structured handoff bundle'
M1-D1 mentions only 'Validated plan_package_final.json accepted and recorded' (no explicit handoff bundle validation/recording deliverable)

findings.summary: Sample check R2: repo_context.json minimum required fields include language (and/or explicit ecosystem metadata) in addition to build-system entrypoints, but milestone/AT2 descriptions do not explicitly require a language field; this may leave the repo_context schema under-specified relative to R2.

evidence.note: M1-D2 lists repo root, build entrypoints, validator entrypoints, protected/forbidden paths, branch/commit metadata; does not explicitly mention language metadata
AT2 required-fields parenthetical mirrors M1-D2 and does not explicitly include language metadata

findings.summary: Sample check R3: R3 states workspace_context.json must be required before any workspace-writing stage begins, but the Intake stage tool policy allows workspace_write (noncanonical-only). Unless clarified that workspace writes are forbidden until workspace_context is validated (or that Intake does not write at all), this is a potential ordering/policy mismatch for the sample check.

evidence.note: R3 requires workspace_context.json before any workspace-writing stage begins
Intake HITL trigger includes missing workspace_context.json, but policy still indicates workspace_write is permitted in Intake
